chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, who said:

I was walking with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so the strap of his sandal broke. I took out a strap from my sleeve and he repaired his sandal with it. Then he struck his hand on my left shoulder and said: 'O Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir! Whoever supports a believer upon the strap of his sandal, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will carry him upon a red camel when he emerges from his grave until he knocks at the door of Paradise.'

key_terms.شِسْعُ: The strap or thong of a sandal
key_terms.نَاقَةٍ دَمْكَاءَ: A red camel (specifically one with a red coat)
key_terms.يَقْرَعَ: To knock or strike (as at a door)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for helping a believer with a minor physical need?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the spiritual weight of minor acts of service by repairing his sandal with the help of Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir. The Imam promises that assisting a believer in such humble needs results in being carried by Allah on a 'damkah' (red) camel from the grave to the gates of Paradise, emphasizing the continuity of reward from death to the afterlife. This narrative underscores the Shia emphasis on practical, everyday kindness as a means of securing divine favor and ease in the Hereafter.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, form Ali Bin Hassan, form Abdul Rahman Bin Kaseer who said,

‘I was walking along with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so the strap of his<sup>asws</sup> sandal got cut (broke). So I took out a strap from my bag and he<sup>asws</sup> repaired his<sup>asws</sup> sandal by it, then struck his<sup>asws</sup> hand upon my left shoulder and said: ‘O Abdul Rahman Bin Kaseyr! The one who supports a Believer upon a strap of his sandal, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would Carry him upon a fast camel when he comes out from his grave until he knocks the door of the Paradise’.
en.sarwar: 13. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir who has said the following:

“I once was walking with abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when the thong and strap of his shoe broke. I took out one from my bag with which he repaired his shoe. He (the Imam) touched my left shoulder saying, ‘O ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, if one helps a believing person in the matters of his shoe thong Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, will carry him on a fast running camel when he comes out of his grave until he will knock at the door of the garden (paradises).”’
